basis: Cavernous vascular tumor arising in the face; facial location alone does not establish cutaneous origin.

decisions.dermatologic: none: face includes several tissues; neither the definition nor the broader concept establishes skin or subcutaneous origin.

basis: Partial phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency; sustained untreated phenylalanine of 600-1200 umol/L causes neurocognitive impairment in roughly >=30%; early treatment can prevent injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: sustained untreated phenylalanine at 600-1200 umol/L commonly causes cognitive dysfunction, estimated >=30%; prevention by treatment does not exclude it.

basis: Hereditary HLH causes immune dysregulation and cytopenias; inflammatory liver injury occurs in >50% and CNS involvement in ~30-50%; extrapolated because RHOG-specific data are limited.

decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS inflammation affects approximately 30-50% in hereditary HLH; applying the parent disease's course, with limited RHOG-specific evidence.

basis: Core autoinflammation, panniculitis/lipodystrophy and myositis/contractures; autoimmune hemolytic anemia 1/1. Neurologic abnormalities, also 1/1, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myositis, muscle atrophy and contractures, each reported in 1/1, form a core muscle phenotype of this proteasome-associated syndrome.

basis: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 20/21; muscle pathology in only 2/2 assessed patients does not establish skeletal involvement in >=30% across the subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: direct myopathy is documented, but 1-2 muscle-assessed cases do not establish >=30% prevalence across the broader cardiomyopathy subtype.

basis: Defining developmental disability; optic hypoplasia/atrophy 80-99% with visual impairment 6/9; hydronephrosis and structural foot deformity each 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: metatarsus adductus is a direct structural foot deformity annotated as frequent (30-79%), meeting the supplied frequency threshold.

basis: Defining bradykinin-mediated edema affects subcutis, bowel and upper airway; C1-inhibitor dysfunction does not itself establish infection, immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway edema is explicitly part of the disease definition and can directly obstruct breathing.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: visceral, characteristically bowel-wall, edema is a defining disease manifestation with impaired digestive function.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: attacks result from bradykinin excess; complement-regulator dysfunction alone does not establish an infectious, immunodeficient or immune-mediated mechanism.

basis: Inherited hepatobiliary bile-acid handling disorder; fat malabsorption reflects altered bile availability without established intestinal injury. Rickets frequency is unspecified.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption and steatorrhea reflect impaired bile availability; direct intestinal damage or an intrinsic intestinal absorptive defect is not established.

basis: Defined by adrenal chromaffin and autonomic paraganglial tumors; renal carcinoma and GIST are separate tumor risks, and common lasting ear damage is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: primary: paragangliomas arise in autonomic paraganglia, supported by the autonomic nervous system neoplasm ancestry; tumor origin qualifies without separate nerve injury.

basis: Lysosomal lipid-storage disorder with defining juvenile neurodegeneration; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish common hepatic or hematologic functional damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic storage and enlargement are common, but damaging hypersplenism or other hematologic dysfunction in >=30% is not established for this juvenile subtype.
